knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Program and Canonical Inequality Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and inequality-form representation of a finite-dimensional linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear program maximizes a prescribed linear function over the vectors satisfying a prescribed system of linear equations and inequalities. Every such linear program can be transformed into the form \[\max_{x\in\mathbb R^n} c^T x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\le b,\] where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear program maximizes a given linear function over vectors satisfying a given system of linear equations and inequalities. Every linear program can be transformed into maximization form with objective c-transpose x and constraints Ax less than or equal to b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The linear program admits the equivalent form }\max\{c^Tx:x\in\mathbb R^n,\ Ax\le b\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Objective Assumption
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of an LP payoff from signed activity contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If activity \(j\), operated at level \(x_j\), contributes \(c_j\) units of the payoff item per unit of activity, then the total payoff is \[z=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jx_j=c^\top x.\] Positive coefficients represent production of the payoff item and negative coefficients represent its consumption; the stated objective is to maximize \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity makes a signed payoff contribution proportional to its level, and total payoff is the sum of those contributions. Positive coefficients produce payoff, negative coefficients consume it, and the objective is to maximize the resulting linear function.
assumptions_latex: x_j\text{ is the level of activity }j
c_j\text{ is its signed payoff contribution per unit of activity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z=c^\top x=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jx_j,\qquad \operatorname*{maximize}\;z.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear objective and maximization-to-minimization conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a linear objective and the sign reversal that converts maximization to minimization without asserting attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activity vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^N\) and coefficients \(c\in\mathbb{R}^N\), the linear form \(z=c^{\mathsf T}x\) is a linear objective function. For any feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^N\) and \(p\in\mathbb{R}^N\), maximizing \(p^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing \((-p)^{\mathsf T}x\) over the same set: \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}p^{\mathsf T}x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(-p)^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad \sup_{x\in F}p^{\mathsf T}x=-\inf_{x\in F}(-p)^{\mathsf T}x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective is a linear form in the activity levels. Maximizing a linear form over a feasible set is equivalent to minimizing its negative over the same set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z=c^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad \operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}p^{\mathsf T}x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(-p)^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad \sup_{x\in F}p^{\mathsf T}x=-\inf_{x\in F}(-p)^{\mathsf T}x.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Coefficient Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-vector representation of a finite-dimensional linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a decision vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), objective coefficient data are a vector \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n\). They determine the linear objective function \(f_c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) by \[f_c(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jx_j.\] Thus \(c_j\) is the marginal coefficient multiplying variable \(x_j\); the optimization sense is separate data and is not encoded by \(c\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coefficient vector c specifies the linear objective cᵀx; each component multiplies one decision variable, while minimization or maximization is specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_c(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x\)

children.title: Minimization Sense
children.top_down_role: Model representations using minimization as the declared optimization sense.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\iff (\forall x\in F)\;c^{\mathsf T}x^\star\le c^{\mathsf T}x\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization semantics for a finite-dimensional linear objective over a feasible set.

source_refs.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set, and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The minimization-sense problem is \[v_{\min}=\inf_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x.\] A point \(x^\star\in F\) is an optimal solution precisely when \(c^{\mathsf T}x^\star\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in F\). If such a point exists, the infimum is attained and \(v_{\min}=c^{\mathsf T}x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization LP in a finite-dimensional decision space seeks a feasible point whose objective value is no greater than that of every other feasible point.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimization Sense

source_witnesses.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

children.title: Maximization Sense
children.top_down_role: Model representations using maximization as the declared optimization sense.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\iff (\forall x\in F)\;c^{\mathsf T}x^\star\ge c^{\mathsf T}x\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization semantics for a finite-dimensional linear objective over a feasible set.

source_refs.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set, and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The maximization-sense problem is \[v_{\max}=\sup_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x.\] A point \(x^\star\in F\) is an optimal solution precisely when \(c^{\mathsf T}x^\star\ge c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in F\). If such a point exists, the supremum is attained and \(v_{\max}=c^{\mathsf T}x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximization LP in a finite-dimensional decision space seeks a feasible point whose objective value is no less than that of every other feasible point.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximization Sense

source_witnesses.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

children.title: Objective-Sense Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between opposite optimization senses under objective sign reversal.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(-c)^{\mathsf T}x\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equivalence obtained by negating all objective coefficients.

source_refs.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), nonempty feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and coefficient vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), maximizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing \((-c)^{\mathsf T}x\) over the same set. Specifically, \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(-c)^{\mathsf T}x.\] With extended-real optimal values, \(\sup_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=-\inf_{x\in F}(-c)^{\mathsf T}x\). Feasibility and attainment are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite-dimensional linear model, negating the objective coefficients converts maximization to minimization without changing the feasible or optimal solution sets; the optimal value changes sign.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Sense Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear models whose task is feasibility rather than objective optimization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), and let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set of a finite linear constraint system. A pure feasibility model asks whether \(F\) is empty and, if it is not, requests any point \(x\in F\). No preference ordering is imposed on feasible points. Equivalently, it may be written as an optimization problem with the identically zero objective: \[\min_{x\in F}0.\] Its admissible outcomes are a feasible point when one exists or a determination that \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional pure feasibility model asks for any point satisfying the linear constraints, or a determination that none exists, without ranking feasible points.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure Feasibility Models

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

children.title: Constant-Objective Models
children.top_down_role: LP instances whose objective value is identical across the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}f(x)=F\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional optimization models whose objective is constant throughout the feasible set.

source_refs.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). An optimization model has a constant objective on \(F\) if there exists \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(f(x)=\alpha\) for every \(x\in F\). For a linear objective \(f(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), this means \(c^{\mathsf T}x=\alpha\) throughout \(F\); the special choice \(c=0\) gives \(\alpha=0\). When \(F\ne\varnothing\), every feasible point is optimal in either optimization sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-objective model in a finite-dimensional decision space assigns the same value to every feasible point, so every feasible point is optimal whenever the model is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Objective Models

source_witnesses.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

children.title: Feasibility–Optimality Collapse
children.top_down_role: Solution-set consequences when every feasible point has the same objective value.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}f(x)\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coincidence of feasible and optimal sets under a constant objective in finite dimension.

source_refs.locator: ONE: INTRODUCTION p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) is constant. If \(F\ne\varnothing\), then every feasible point attains both the minimum and maximum objective values, so the feasible set, minimizer set, and maximizer set coincide: \[F=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}f(x).\] Consequently, finding an optimal solution reduces exactly to finding a feasible point. If \(F=\varnothing\), there is neither a feasible nor an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a constant objective on a finite-dimensional feasible set, feasibility and optimality coincide: every feasible point is both a minimizer and a maximizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Optimality Collapse

\text{Each successive pair differs by insertion or deletion of an equation redundant at that step.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal E_0\sim\mathcal E_r.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix and rowwise forms of finite linear equality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite linear equality system in \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is specified by \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and has the form \[Ax=b.\] Its feasible set is \(F_{=}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\). Equivalently, if \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\) is row \(i\) of \(A\), then feasibility requires \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Each equality confines \(x\) to an affine hyperplane unless its row is degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality system requires every linear row expression to equal its specified right-hand side, defining an intersection of affine hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{=}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\)

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Inequality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear systems imposing one upper or lower bound per row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A one-sided linear inequality system in \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) assigns each row one comparison direction. In uniform upper-bound form, data \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) define \[Ax\le b,\qquad F_{\le}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\},\] where inequalities are componentwise. A lower-bound row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\) is equivalently written \((-a_i)^{\mathsf T}x\le -b_i\). Thus either direction describes a closed halfspace, and the system describes their intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each one-sided inequality places either an upper or lower bound on one linear row expression; the feasible set is the intersection of the resulting halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\le}=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\}\)

notation.meaning: row i of the coefficient matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source's convention that an unqualified linear inequality is non-strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear inequality in variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is a relation \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\), as distinguished from the strict linear inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i<b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear inequality is a non-strict relation a_1x_1+...+a_nx_n ≤ b, as opposed to the strict relation a_1x_1+...+a_nx_n < b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\text{ is a linear inequality, whereas }\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i<b\text{ is strict.}

children.title: Ranged Rows
children.top_down_role: Constraint rows carrying both lower and upper activity limits.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell\le a^{\mathsf T}x\le u\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\le u\}\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:(-a)^{\mathsf T}x\le-\ell\}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional linear row carrying simultaneous finite lower and upper bounds.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\). A ranged row for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) consists of a coefficient vector \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and finite bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}\) with \(\ell<u\), imposing \[\ell\le a^{\mathsf T}x\le u.\] It is exactly the conjunction of the two one-sided inequalities \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le u\) and \((-a)^{\mathsf T}x\le-\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranged row in a finite-dimensional linear system simultaneously lower- and upper-bounds one linear expression and is equivalent to two one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Ranged Rows

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

children.title: Mixed-Sense Row Systems
children.top_down_role: Systems combining equality, upper-bounded, lower-bounded, or ranged row types.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\forall i\in I,\ a_i^{\mathsf T}x\mathrel{\sigma_i}b_i\}\), where \(\sigma_i\in\{=,\le,\ge\}\) is fixed by the partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear systems combining equality, upper-bound, and lower-bound rows.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), and let the finite row index set \(I\) be partitioned into disjoint sets \(I_=\), \(I_\le\), and \(I_\ge\). Given \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(i\in I\), a mixed-sense linear row system requires, for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\ \ (i\in I_=),\qquad a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\ \ (i\in I_\le),\qquad a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\ \ (i\in I_\ge).\] Multiplying every lower-bound row by \(-1\) converts the system to an equivalent combination of equality and upper-bound rows without changing its feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional mixed-sense system combines equality, less-than-or-equal, and greater-than-or-equal rows, with each row assigned exactly one sense.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Sense Row Systems

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-intersection representation induced by a finite partition of finite-dimensional constraint rows.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,k\in\mathbb{N}\). Let \(I\) be the finite index set of a linear row system, and let \(I_1,\ldots,I_k\) be a disjoint partition of \(I\) by row type, such as equality, upper-bound, lower-bound, or ranged. For every \(r\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), define \(F_r\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) to be the set of points satisfying every row indexed by \(I_r\). Then the full feasible set has the representation \[F=\bigcap_{r=1}^k F_r.\] Every row appears in exactly one block, while a point is feasible precisely when it belongs to every block-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional row system partitioned into finitely many row-type blocks, the overall feasible set is the intersection of the sets satisfying the individual blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Type Partitioning

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Restricted Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar LP variables constrained to one closed half-line through zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar decision variable is sign-restricted when its domain is either \([0,\infty)\) or \(( -\infty,0]\). Thus a nonnegative variable satisfies \(x\ge 0\), while a nonpositive variable satisfies \(x\le 0\). A nonpositive variable may be replaced by \(z=-x\), where \(z\ge 0\), without changing the represented feasible decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign-restricted variable is constrained to be nonnegative or nonpositive; negating a nonpositive variable converts it to a nonnegative one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in[0,\infty)\) or \(x\in(-\infty,0]\).

notation.meaning: Equivalent nonnegative replacement for a nonpositive variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Free Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestricted scalar variables and their standard sign-restricted representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar decision variable \(x\) is free, or unrestricted in sign, when its domain is all of \(\mathbb{R}\). It admits the standard representation \(x=x^+-x^-\), where \(x^+\ge 0\) and \(x^-\ge 0\). Every real value of \(x\) has such a representation, although the representing pair need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free variable may take any real value and can be represented as the difference of two nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), equivalently \(x=x^+-x^-\) for some \(x^+,x^-\ge 0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Free variables in a linear program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines free LP variables and presents an LP formulation containing nonnegative and free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable \(z\) is free if it has no explicit lower or upper bound. An LP with nonnegative variables \(x\) and free variables \(z\) can be formulated as \[\min_{x,z}\;c^Tx+d^Tz\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Cz=b,\qquad x\ge 0,\] where no bound or sign restriction is imposed on \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free variable has no explicit lower or upper bound. An LP may contain nonnegative variables x and free variables z, with no bound or sign restriction imposed on z.

knowledge_statements.title: General Mixed Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LP allowing mixed row relations and variable sign or bound restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A general mixed-form linear program has the form
\[\operatorname{opt}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_{\le}x\le b_{\le},\quad A_{=}x=b_{=},\quad A_{\ge}x\ge b_{\ge},\quad \ell\le x\le u,\]
where \(\operatorname{opt}\in\{\min,\max\}\). A component \(\ell_j=-\infty\) removes the lower bound on \(x_j\), and a component \(u_j=+\infty\) removes its upper bound. Empty row blocks are permitted. Its feasible set consists of all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying every displayed row and bound restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-form LP permits minimization or maximization, equality and either inequality orientation, and variables that are bounded, one-sided, nonnegative, nonpositive, or free.
assumptions_latex: All matrix blocks have \(n\) columns and compatible right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_{\le}x\le b_{\le},\ A_=x=b_=,\ A_{\ge}x\ge b_{\ge},\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral geometry determined directly by mixed row senses and variable bounds.

The feasible set \(F\) of a general mixed-form LP is a closed convex polyhedron. If \(F\ne\varnothing\), then

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Mixed-Form Linear Program and Basic Solution Terminology
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a general linear program with mixed constraint senses and sign restrictions, including feasibility, optimality, unboundedness below, and conversion of maximization to minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), finite index sets \(M_1,M_2,M_3\), data \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}\), and sets \(N_1,N_2\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), a general linear program has the form
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}c^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\begin{cases}
a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i,&i\in M_1,\\
a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i,&i\in M_2,\\
a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i,&i\in M_3,\\
x_j\ge0,&j\in N_1,\\
x_j\le0,&j\in N_2.
\end{cases}
\]
A vector satisfying all constraints is feasible, and the collection of feasible vectors is the feasible set \(F\). If \(j\notin N_1\cup N_2\), then \(x_j\) is free. A feasible vector \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in F\). The cost is unbounded below if and only if, for every \(K\in\mathbb{R}\), some \(x\in F\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}x<K\); equivalently, \(\inf_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=-\infty\). Maximizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing \(-c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general mixed-form linear program minimizes a linear objective subject to finite collections of linear inequalities and equalities and specified variable-sign restrictions. Vectors satisfying every constraint are feasible, and a variable without either sign restriction is free. A feasible vector is optimal when no feasible vector has lower cost. The cost is unbounded below when feasible costs fall below every real threshold. Maximization is converted to minimization by negating the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in F\text{ is optimal}\iff (\forall x\in F)\ c^{\mathsf T}x^*\le c^{\mathsf T}x;\qquad \inf_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=-\infty\iff(\forall K\in\mathbb{R})(\exists x\in F)\ c^{\mathsf T}x<K.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Form equivalence for an inequality-form minimization problem with unrestricted variables; the construction preserves feasibility under projection and preserves objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), with \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) unrestricted in sign. The problem \[\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\le b\}\] is equivalently represented by \[\inf\left\{\begin{bmatrix}c\\-c\\0\end{bmatrix}^{T}\begin{bmatrix}x^+\\x^-\\z\end{bmatrix}:\begin{bmatrix}A&-A&I\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x^+\\x^-\\z\end{bmatrix}=b,\ x^+,x^-,z\ge0\right\},\] under the projection \(x=x^+-x^-\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an LP with constraints Ax ≤ b and unrestricted variables, introduce a nonnegative slack z and replace each free variable x by x+ − x− with x+ and x− nonnegative. The resulting equality-constrained problem has only nonnegative variables, projects onto exactly the original feasible set, and preserves objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Inequality Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical all-inequality presentations of a finite-dimensional LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An LP in canonical maximization inequality form is
\[\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}.\]
Its sign-reversed minimization presentation is
\[\min\{(-c)^{\mathsf T}x:(-A)x\ge-b,\ x\ge0\}.\]
The two programs have the same feasible vectors, and their objective values at every feasible \(x\) are negatives of one another. Thus an optimizer of either program is an optimizer of the other after reversing the objective sense and sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical maximization uses nonnegative variables and less-than rows; simultaneous sign reversal yields an equivalent minimization with greater-than rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}=-\min\{(-c)^{\mathsf T}x:(-A)x\ge-b,\ x\ge0\}\), whenever the optimal values are defined in the extended-real sense.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical minimization-form LP, its data, and feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional minimization LP with componentwise nonnegative variables and greater-than-or-equal constraints; no feasibility, boundedness, or attainment is presumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For data \(A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), the displayed linear program is \(\inf\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\). Here \(c^\top x\) is the objective function, \(A\) is the constraint matrix, and \(b\) is the right-hand-side vector. A vector \(x\) is feasible if and only if \(Ax\ge b\) and \(x\ge0\), and the feasible region is \(\mathcal F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\). If the infimum is attained, an optimal solution is a feasible vector minimizing \(c^\top x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the displayed canonical minimization form, an LP has a linear objective, greater-than-or-equal linear constraints, and nonnegative variables. The technological coefficients form the constraint matrix, and the right-hand side specifies the requirements. A feasible solution satisfies all constraints, and the feasible region is the set of all such solutions. The formulation alone does not guarantee feasibility, boundedness, or attainment.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R^m,\quad c\in\mathbb R^n
Ax\ge b\text{ and }x\ge0\text{ are interpreted componentwise}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \inf_{x\in\mathcal F}c^\top x

children.title: Equality Row Structure
children.top_down_role: The equality-constrained row component of standard-form LP representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Row Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine geometry induced by the equality block in standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a standard-form constraint system \(Ax=b\), the equality rows define the affine set
\[H=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}.\]
If the system is consistent and \(x_0\in H\), then \(H=x_0+\ker A\). Consequently, if \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\), the affine dimension of \(H\) is \(n-r\). Removing linearly dependent equality rows does not change \(H\), provided the corresponding right-hand-side equations are redundant rather than inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistent equality rows define an affine translate of the matrix nullspace, with dimension equal to the number of variables minus the matrix rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=x_0+\ker A\) and \(\dim H=n-\operatorname{rank}(A)\) for every \(x_0\in H\).

notation.meaning: Affine solution set of the equality rows

source_refs.locator: Standard Form p. 22

source_witnesses.locator: Standard Form p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality-System Consistency Alternative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent consistency tests and an explicit certificate for failure of an equality-row system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[Ax=b\text{ is consistent}\iff \operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}([A\ b])\iff (A^{\mathsf T}y=0\Rightarrow b^{\mathsf T}y=0).\]
Consequently, \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) with
\[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0.\]
Such a certificate can be rescaled so that \(b^{\mathsf T}y=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality system is consistent exactly when augmenting its matrix by the right-hand side does not increase rank, equivalently when every left-null vector is orthogonal to the right-hand side. A violating left-null vector certifies inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent iff \(\exists y:A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\).

notation.meaning: Matrix obtained by appending b to A

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-System Consistency Alternative

children.title: Nonnegative Variable Domain
children.top_down_role: The componentwise nonnegative domain used by standard-form variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Variable Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-domain component of standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonnegative variable domain in \(n\) dimensions is the closed convex cone
\[\mathbb R_+^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_j\ge0\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,n\}.\]
In standard-form linear programming, feasibility requires membership in this cone in addition to satisfaction of the equality rows. Zero components are allowed; strict positivity is not part of the domain definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard-form variables belong to the nonnegative orthant: every component is at least zero, and zero components are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\iff x_j\ge0\) for all \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative orthant in n-dimensional real space

source_refs.locator: Standard Form p. 22

source_witnesses.locator: Standard Form p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-Duality of the Nonnegative Orthant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone representation under the standard Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With
\[K^*=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\},\]
the nonnegative orthant is self-dual:
\[(\mathbb R_+^n)^*=\mathbb R_+^n.\]
Equivalently, \(y^{\mathsf T}x\ge0\) for every \(x\ge0\) if and only if \(y\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the nonnegative-pairing convention, the dual cone of the nonnegative orthant is the nonnegative orthant itself.
assumptions_latex: Dual cones use the displayed nonnegative-pairing convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathbb R_+^n)^*=\mathbb R_+^n\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of K under the stated convention

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Duality of the Nonnegative Orthant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral and Facial Geometry of the Nonnegative Orthant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic cone, ray, and face structure of the standard-form variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonnegative orthant \(\mathbb R_+^n\) is a closed, convex, polyhedral, pointed, full-dimensional cone generated by the coordinate vectors:
\[\mathbb R_+^n=\operatorname{cone}\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}.\]
Its extreme rays are exactly \(\{\lambda e_j:\lambda\ge0\}\). Every face has the form
\[F_I=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:x_i=0\text{ for every }i\in I\}\]
for some \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative orthant is a pointed full-dimensional polyhedral cone generated by the coordinate axes; its extreme rays are those axes and its faces arise by setting selected coordinates to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R_+^n=\operatorname{cone}\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\), with the stated extreme rays and faces.

notation.meaning: Coordinate face indexed by coordinates fixed to zero

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral and Facial Geometry of the Nonnegative Orthant

children.title: Standard-Form Coupling
children.top_down_role: Joint structural role of equality rows with nonnegative variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling of affine equality rows with the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A minimization linear program is in standard form when it is written as
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad x\ge0.\]
The equality-row and variable-domain conditions are jointly imposed, so its feasible region is
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\cap\mathbb R_+^n.\]
Thus standard-form feasibility is the intersection of an affine set with the nonnegative orthant, not either condition separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard-form LP minimizes a linear objective over the intersection of equality rows and the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x:Ax=b\}\cap\mathbb R_+^n\), and the program is \(\min_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\).

source_refs.locator: Standard Form p. 22

source_witnesses.locator: Standard Form p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession and Lineality of a Standard-Form Feasible Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry produced specifically by intersecting equality rows with the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}.\]
If \(P\ne\varnothing\), then
\[\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Ad=0,\ d\ge0\}.\]
Moreover,
\[\operatorname{lin}(P)=\operatorname{rec}(P)\cap(-\operatorname{rec}(P))=\{0\}.\]
Thus every nonempty standard-form feasible region is pointed, although it is unbounded whenever a nonzero \(d\ge0\) satisfies \(Ad=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession directions of a nonempty standard-form feasible region are precisely the nonnegative null vectors of A. Its lineality space is zero, so it is pointed even when unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\ker(A)\cap\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(\operatorname{lin}(P)=\{0\}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Recession and Lineality of a Standard-Form Feasible Region

children.title: Standard-Form Data Layout
children.top_down_role: Matrix, right-hand-side, and objective data organization for this canonical form.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Data Layout
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensions and storage roles of standard-form LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard-form program
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\]
the data layout is \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), while the decision vector is \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Each row of \(A\), paired with the corresponding component of \(b\), specifies one equality; each column of \(A\), paired with the corresponding component of \(c\), represents one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard-form data consist of an m-by-n constraint matrix, an m-vector right-hand side, and an n-vector objective, with one matrix column per variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c,x\in\mathbb R^n\), with conformable products \(Ax\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).

source_refs.locator: Storing the Problem Data: Dimension and Size p. 51

source_witnesses.locator: Storing the Problem Data: Dimension and Size p. 51

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP form with explicit finite or extended-real componentwise bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bounded-variable linear program has the form
\[\operatorname{opt}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad \ell\le x\le u,\]
where \(\operatorname{opt}\in\{\min,\max\}\), inequalities are componentwise, and \(\ell_j\le u_j\) for every \(j\). Finite \(\ell_j,u_j\) give a two-sided bounded variable; \(\ell_j=0\) and \(u_j=+\infty\) give a nonnegative variable; and \(\ell_j=-\infty\), \(u_j=+\infty\) give a free variable. The feasible region is the affine equality set intersected with the componentwise bound set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-variable form combines equality rows with explicit componentwise lower and upper bounds, including one-sided and free-variable cases through the appropriate infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).

notation.meaning: Lower and upper bounds for variable j

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite Endpoints Remove the General Compactness Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for compactness and bounded objectives when extended endpoints are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With no effective equality rows and \(0\le x\le+\infty\), the feasible set is \(F=[0,\infty)\). It is noncompact, and \(\max\{x:x\in F\}\) is unbounded above. Thus an infinite endpoint removes the blanket compactness and finite-attainment guarantee, although particular instances with infinite endpoints may still have optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-sided variable can yield a noncompact feasible set and an unbounded objective.
assumptions_latex: There are no effective equality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=[0,\infty)\text{ is noncompact and }\sup_{x\in F}x=+\infty.

notation.meaning: absence of a finite upper bound

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Endpoints Remove the General Compactness Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Bound Compactness and Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric consequence when every variable has two finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), where \(l,u\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(l\le u\). Then \(F\) is compact. Consequently, if \(F\ne\varnothing\), every linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) attains finite minimum and maximum values on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty equality-constrained finite box is compact, so every linear objective has finite attained extrema.
assumptions_latex: \(l\le u\) and all endpoints are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is compact, and if nonempty then }\min_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\text{ and }\max_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x\text{ are finite and attained.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Bound Compactness and Attainment

children.title: Objective-Sense Conversions
children.top_down_role: Representation changes between minimization and maximization conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Sense Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion between minimization and maximization objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), replacing maximization by minimization of the negated objective preserves all feasible vectors and optimizers:
\[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(-c)^{\mathsf T}x.\]
The optimal values satisfy
\[\sup_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=-\inf_{x\in F}(-c)^{\mathsf T}x\]
in the extended-real sense. Applying the conversion twice restores the original objective sense and coefficient vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating every objective coefficient converts maximization to minimization, or conversely, without changing feasible points or optimizers; the optimal value changes sign.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the unchanged feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\max_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x=\arg\min_{x\in F}(-c)^{\mathsf T}x\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set, unchanged by objective conversion

children.title: Row-Orientation Conversions
children.top_down_role: Representation changes between opposite inequality orientations.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Orientation Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-reversal equivalence for individual linear constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), multiplying both sides of a row by \(-1\) reverses its inequality orientation:
\[a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\iff(-a)^{\mathsf T}x\ge-b,\qquad a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\iff(-a)^{\mathsf T}x\le-b.\]
For equality rows,
\[a^{\mathsf T}x=b\iff(-a)^{\mathsf T}x=-b.\]
Hence row sign reversal leaves the represented feasible set unchanged and is an involution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying a constraint row and its right-hand side by negative one reverses an inequality or preserves equality without changing its solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed row and its sign-reversed counterpart define the same subset of \(\mathbb R^n\).

children.title: Conversion Composition
children.top_down_role: Combined use of sense reversal with row reorientation in canonicalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Conversion Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition law for independent objective- and row-orientation sign conversions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_o\) negate the objective coefficients and reverse the optimization sense, and let \(T_i\) negate selected constraint rows and reverse their inequality orientations. Each transformation is an involution: \(T_o^2=T_i^2=I\). Because \(T_o\) changes only the objective and \(T_i\) changes only selected constraint representations, they commute:
\[T_oT_i=T_iT_o.\]
Every composition preserves the optimizer set after accounting for objective-value sign, and every row conversion preserves the feasible set exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective sign conversion and row sign conversion are commuting involutions; composing them in either order yields the same LP representation and optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: All transformed objective coefficients, row coefficients, right-hand sides, senses, and orientations are changed together as specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_o^2=T_i^2=I\) and \(T_oT_i=T_iT_o\).

children.title: Slack-Variable Conversions
children.top_down_role: Equality-form representations of upper-oriented inequality rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between a less-than row and an equality with nonnegative slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), introduce a slack variable \(s\in\mathbb R_+\) and replace the row by
\[a^{\mathsf T}x+s=b,\qquad s\ge0.\]
For every \(x\), the original inequality holds if and only if there exists exactly one such slack, namely
\[s=b-a^{\mathsf T}x.\]
Thus projection of the augmented equality system onto the original \(x\)-space recovers precisely the original feasible set, while the objective remains unchanged when the coefficient of \(s\) is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A less-than constraint is equivalent to an equality after adding a uniquely determined nonnegative slack variable with zero objective coefficient.
assumptions_latex: The added variable has objective coefficient \(0\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\iff\exists!s\ge0:\ a^{\mathsf T}x+s=b\), with \(s=b-a^{\mathsf T}x\).

children.title: Surplus-Variable Conversions
children.top_down_role: Equality-form representations of lower-oriented inequality rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Surplus-Variable Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between a greater-than row and an equality with nonnegative surplus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\), introduce a surplus variable \(t\in\mathbb R_+\) and replace the row by
\[a^{\mathsf T}x-t=b,\qquad t\ge0.\]
For every \(x\), the original inequality holds if and only if there exists exactly one such surplus, namely
\[t=a^{\mathsf T}x-b.\]
Thus projection of the augmented equality system onto the original \(x\)-space recovers precisely the original feasible set, while the objective remains unchanged when the coefficient of \(t\) is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A greater-than constraint is equivalent to an equality after subtracting a uniquely determined nonnegative surplus variable with zero objective coefficient.
assumptions_latex: The added variable has objective coefficient \(0\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\iff\exists!t\ge0:\ a^{\mathsf T}x-t=b\), with \(t=a^{\mathsf T}x-b\).

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Sign Domains
children.top_down_role: Domain conventions attached to row-conversion variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Sign Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign conventions for slack and surplus variables attached to scalar LP rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a scalar affine row with left side \(a^{\mathsf T}x\) and right side \(b\), an inequality is converted to equality using a nonnegative auxiliary variable. Specifically, \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is equivalent to \(a^{\mathsf T}x+s=b\) with \(s\ge0\), while \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) is equivalent to \(a^{\mathsf T}x-s=b\) with \(s\ge0\). Equivalently, if the second conversion is written \(a^{\mathsf T}x+u=b\), then \(u\le0\). The auxiliary sign domain is therefore determined by its algebraic orientation in the equality, not merely by the row direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A less-than row adds a nonnegative slack; a greater-than row subtracts a nonnegative surplus, or equivalently adds a nonpositive auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\iff\exists s\ge0:\ a^{\mathsf T}x+s=b\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\iff\exists s\ge0:\ a^{\mathsf T}x-s=b\).

notation.meaning: Signed auxiliary variable when added to the row.

children.title: Row-Recovery Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original inequality rows from equality-form representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Recovery Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between feasible original rows and their equality-plus-slack formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), define its slack by \(s=b-a^{\mathsf T}x\). Then \(x\) satisfies the original row exactly when the uniquely determined value \(s\) is nonnegative and \((x,s)\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}x+s=b\). Projection of the augmented feasible set onto the \(x\)-coordinates recovers the original feasible set, and the lifting map \(x\mapsto(x,b-a^{\mathsf T}x)\) is its inverse. For \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\), the same correspondence holds with surplus \(s=a^{\mathsf T}x-b\) and equality \(a^{\mathsf T}x-s=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection removes each slack or surplus, while its row residual uniquely reconstructs it; thus the original and augmented feasible sets correspond bijectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto(x,b-a^{\mathsf T}x)\) bijects \(\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\) with \(\{(x,s):a^{\mathsf T}x+s=b,\ s\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: Row residual used as slack or surplus.

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form replacement of one unrestricted scalar variable by two nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) be unrestricted in sign. Introduce \(x_j^+\ge0\) and \(x_j^-\ge0\), and substitute \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) everywhere. In a linear constraint matrix, the original column \(A_{:j}\) is replaced by the two columns \(A_{:j}\) and \(-A_{:j}\); in the objective, coefficient \(c_j\) is replaced by coefficients \(c_j\) and \(-c_j\). Every value of \(x_j\) has such a representation, and the representing pair is generally nonunique. The canonical choices \(x_j^+=\max\{x_j,0\}\) and \(x_j^-=\max\{-x_j,0\}\) are unique, but no complementarity constraint is required for the LP conversion or for equivalence after projection onto the original variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted variable is represented as the difference of two nonnegative variables; its matrix and objective coefficients are duplicated with opposite signs, and the auxiliary pair need not be unique.
assumptions_latex: The model depends linearly on the unrestricted scalar \(x_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\in\mathbb R\iff\exists x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0:\ x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative variables replacing the unrestricted variable.
Constraint-matrix column associated with the original variable.

children.title: Lower-Bound Shifting
children.top_down_role: Variable recentering based on finite lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Shifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of a finite lower bound to nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a scalar variable satisfies the finite lower bound \(x_j\ge\ell_j\). Introduce \(y_j=x_j-\ell_j\), so that \(y_j\ge0\) and \(x_j=\ell_j+y_j\). This substitution is a bijection between the original domain and the nonnegative half-line. In any linear expression \(a^{\mathsf T}x\), replacing \(x_j\) contributes the constant \(a_j\ell_j\) and leaves coefficient \(a_j\) on \(y_j\). Thus feasibility and objective ordering are preserved after the induced constants are transferred to the corresponding right-hand side and objective offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a finite lower bound converts a bounded-below variable into a nonnegative variable, with constants absorbed into rows and the objective offset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\ge\ell_j\iff y_j=x_j-\ell_j\ge0\), with inverse \(x_j=\ell_j+y_j\).

notation.meaning: Finite lower bound on the original variable.

children.title: Upper-Bound Shifting
children.top_down_role: Variable recentering based on finite upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Shifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation and reflection of a finite upper bound to nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a scalar variable satisfies the finite upper bound \(x_j\le u_j\). Introduce \(y_j=u_j-x_j\), so that \(y_j\ge0\) and \(x_j=u_j-y_j\). This substitution bijects the original domain with the nonnegative half-line. In any linear expression \(a^{\mathsf T}x\), the term \(a_jx_j\) becomes \(a_ju_j-a_jy_j\); hence the transformed column and objective coefficient are negated, while the induced constant is transferred to the row right-hand side or objective offset. Feasibility and objective ordering are preserved under the inverse substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a variable from its finite upper bound produces a nonnegative variable and negates its linear coefficients while shifting constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\le u_j\iff y_j=u_j-x_j\ge0\), with inverse \(x_j=u_j-y_j\).

notation.meaning: Finite upper bound on the original variable.

children.title: General Variable Translation
children.top_down_role: Affine coordinate shifts not tied to a single bound orientation.

knowledge_statements.title: General Variable Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible affine change of LP variables and its feasible-set correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=Ty+d\), where \(T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\). Substitution transforms the LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\mathrel{\bowtie}b,\ x\in X\}\) into \(\min\{(T^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}d:ATy\mathrel{\bowtie}b-Ad,\ Ty+d\in X\}\), with each component of \(\mathrel{\bowtie}\) retaining its original relation. The map \(y\mapsto Ty+d\) bijects the transformed and original feasible sets. For corresponding points, \((T^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}d=c^{\mathsf T}(Ty+d)\), so the substitution preserves objective values, optimal values, attainment, and unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine substitution bijects feasible sets, right-multiplies the constraint matrix, shifts right-hand sides, and transforms the objective coefficients and offset while preserving corresponding objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(b\), \(c\), \(d\), and the domain \(X\) have compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=Ty+d\) gives a bijective, objective-value-preserving equivalence between the displayed original and transformed LPs.

notation.meaning: Nonsingular linear part of the variable transformation.
Componentwise collection of equality or inequality relations.

children.title: Translation Effects on Model Data
children.top_down_role: Changes to row constants, objective offsets, and domain descriptions under translation.

knowledge_statements.title: Translation Effects on Model Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-level update formulas for an affine change of LP variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the substitution \(x=Ty+d\), an affine constraint system \(Ax\mathrel{\bowtie}b\) becomes \((AT)y\mathrel{\bowtie}b-Ad\). An affine objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma\) becomes \((T^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}y+(\gamma+c^{\mathsf T}d)\). Thus the transformed matrix, right-hand side, objective vector, and objective constant are respectively \(A'=AT\), \(b'=b-Ad\), \(c'=T^{\mathsf T}c\), and \(\gamma'=\gamma+c^{\mathsf T}d\). For a pure translation, \(T=I\), so variable coefficients are unchanged and only right-hand sides and constant terms move.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine substitution updates LP data by explicit matrix formulas; a pure translation changes right-hand sides and offsets but not variable coefficients.
assumptions_latex: All matrices and vectors have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A'=AT\), \(b'=b-Ad\), \(c'=T^{\mathsf T}c\), and \(\gamma'=\gamma+c^{\mathsf T}d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact removal of variables whose lower and upper bounds coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the variables as \(x=(x_F,x_R)\) and suppose the fixed block is constrained by \(x_F=\bar x_F\). For the LP with rows \(A_Fx_F+A_Rx_R\mathrel{\bowtie}b\) and objective \(c_F^{\mathsf T}x_F+c_R^{\mathsf T}x_R+\gamma\), eliminate \(x_F\) to obtain rows \(A_Rx_R\mathrel{\bowtie}b-A_F\bar x_F\) and objective \(c_R^{\mathsf T}x_R+\gamma+c_F^{\mathsf T}\bar x_F\). Feasible reduced points lift uniquely by adjoining \(\bar x_F\), and every original feasible point projects to a reduced feasible point with the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting fixed values removes their columns, shifts row right-hand sides, and adds their objective contribution to the constant term.
assumptions_latex: The fixed values \(\bar x_F\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_R\mapsto(\bar x_F,x_R)\) bijects the reduced and original feasible sets and preserves objective values.

notation.meaning: Constraint-matrix columns for fixed and retained blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-of-Affine Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear epigraph formulation of a finite maximum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\max_{1\le k\le m}\{a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k\}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(m<\infty\). Its epigraph is the polyhedron \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):t\ge a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k\ \text{for every }k\}\). Consequently, in a minimization model, replacing the term \(f(x)\) by an auxiliary variable \(t\), adding the inequalities \(t\ge a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k\), and minimizing \(t\) with the remaining objective terms is exact: for each fixed feasible \(x\), the smallest admissible \(t\) equals \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph of a finite maximum of affine functions is described by one linear inequality per affine piece, yielding an exact LP formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f=\bigcap_{k=1}^m\{(x,t):t\ge a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k\}\).

notation.meaning: Epigraph variable representing the maximum value.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Representation of Polyhedral Sets p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective-Monotonicity Boundary for Epigraph Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which an epigraph auxiliary equals the represented maximum in a minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\max_k(a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k)\) and minimize \(g(x)+\alpha t\) subject to \(x\in X\) and \(t\ge f(x)\), where \(t\) occurs nowhere else and has no upper bound. If \(\alpha>0\), every attained optimum satisfies \(t=f(x)\). If \(\alpha=0\), optimality need not force equality. If \(\alpha<0\) and some \(x\in X\) has finite \(g(x)\), the lifted problem is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive minimization weight forces an epigraph variable to equal the maximum; zero weight need not, and negative weight makes the unrestricted lift unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(t\) occurs only in the epigraph inequalities and the displayed objective term.
For the negative-weight conclusion, there exists \(x\in X\) with finite \(g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha>0\Rightarrow t=f(x)\text{ at every attained optimum};\quad\alpha=0\text{ need not force equality};\quad\alpha<0\Rightarrow\inf=-\infty.

notation.meaning: Objective coefficient of the epigraph variable.
Feasible set of the original variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Monotonicity Boundary for Epigraph Tightness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Polyhedral Convex Function Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite-maximum and polyhedral-epigraph characterizations for finite-valued functions on finite-dimensional real space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-valued function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), the following are equivalent: \(f\) is polyhedral convex; \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is a polyhedron; and there are finitely many \(a_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_k\in\mathbb R\) such that \(f(x)=\max_{1\le k\le m}(a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued function is polyhedral convex exactly when its epigraph is polyhedral, equivalently when it is a finite maximum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is polyhedral convex}\iff\operatorname{epi}f\text{ is a polyhedron}\iff f(x)=\max_{1\le k\le m}(a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Polyhedral Convex Function Characterization

children.title: Absolute-Value Models
children.top_down_role: LP representations centered on scalar or componentwise absolute-value terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Value Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact LP epigraph and positive-negative-part formulations for scalar absolute values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any affine residual \(r(x)=a^{\mathsf T}x-b\), the constraint \(t\ge|r(x)|\) is equivalent to the two linear inequalities \(t\ge r(x)\) and \(t\ge-r(x)\). Hence minimizing \(|r(x)|\) is represented exactly by minimizing \(t\) subject to those inequalities. Equivalently, one may impose \(r(x)=p-q\) with \(p,q\ge0\) and minimize \(p+q\); at an optimum with a positive coefficient on \(p+q\), its value equals \(|r(x)|\). The epigraph formulation also implies \(t\ge0\) without requiring a separate sign constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute value is modeled by two epigraph inequalities, or by positive and negative residual parts whose sum is minimized.
assumptions_latex: The modeled absolute-value term has a positive minimization weight when using positive and negative parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge|r(x)|\iff t\ge r(x)\ \text{and}\ t\ge-r(x)\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative positive and negative residual parts.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Representation of Polyhedral Sets p. 75

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Representation of Polyhedral Sets p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Sum of Absolute Affine Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact componentwise LP formulation of a finite nonnegative weighted sum of scalar absolute affine residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_i(x)=a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\) and \(w_i\ge0\). Replacing \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i|r_i(x)|\) in a minimization objective by \(\sum_iw_it_i\) together with \(t_i\ge r_i(x)\) and \(t_i\ge-r_i(x)\) preserves the objective infimum and projected optimal \(x\)-solutions. Every coordinate with \(w_i>0\) is tight at an attained optimum. A coordinate with \(w_i=0\) need not be tight; if some \(w_i<0\), the unrestricted epigraph lift is unbounded below whenever the remaining model has a point with finite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of absolute affine residuals is modeled componentwise by two inequalities per residual; positive weights force tightness, zero weights do not, and negative weights make an unrestricted epigraph lift unbounded.
assumptions_latex: Each \(t_i\) occurs only in its epigraph inequalities and the displayed objective term.
The \(t_i\) have no finite upper bounds.
For the negative-weight conclusion, the remaining model has a feasible point with finite objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_x\left(g(x)+\sum_iw_i|r_i(x)|\right)=\inf_{x,t_i\ge\pm r_i(x)}\left(g(x)+\sum_iw_it_i\right)\quad\text{for }w_i\ge0.

notation.meaning: Epigraph variable for the ith absolute residual.
Weight of the ith absolute-value term.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Sum of Absolute Affine Residuals

children.title: Polyhedral-Norm Models
children.top_down_role: LP representations for norms with polyhedral unit balls.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Norm Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum representation and LP epigraph of a norm with polyhedral unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|_P\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\) whose dual unit ball is the polytope \(P^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\). Then \(\|x\|_P=\max_{1\le k\le m}v_k^{\mathsf T}x\). Therefore its epigraph has the finite linear description \(\{(x,t):v_k^{\mathsf T}x\le t\ \text{for all }k\}\). If the listed vertices are not explicitly closed under negation, central symmetry of \(P^\circ\) still ensures that the maximum is nonnegative and equals the norm. Substitution of an affine expression for \(x\) preserves linearity of all epigraph inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral norm is the maximum of finitely many linear functionals from its dual unit ball, so its epigraph is LP-representable.
assumptions_latex: \(P^\circ\subset\mathbb R^n\) is the dual unit ball of a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_P=\max_k v_k^{\mathsf T}x\), and \(t\ge\|x\|_P\iff v_k^{\mathsf T}x\le t\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: Dual unit ball of the polyhedral norm.
A vertex of the dual unit ball.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Representation of Polyhedral Sets p. 75

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Representation of Polyhedral Sets p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-LP Boundary for Norm Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between polyhedral norms and norms admitting finite continuous-LP epigraph formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), its epigraph \(E=\{(x,t):t\geq\|x\|\}\) is a polyhedron if and only if its unit ball \(B=\{x:\|x\|\leq1\}\) is a polytope. Consequently, if \(B\) is nonpolyhedral, then \(E\) has no exact extended formulation using finitely many continuous variables and linear constraints. In particular, for \(n\geq2\), the Euclidean norm has no such formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm has a finite continuous-LP epigraph formulation exactly when its unit ball is polyhedral; the Euclidean norm in dimension at least two is a counterexample.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on finite-dimensional \(\mathbb R^n\).
Extended formulations use finitely many continuous variables and linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\text{ is polyhedral}\iff B\text{ is a polytope};\qquad B\text{ nonpolyhedral}\implies E\text{ has no finite continuous-LP lift}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-LP Boundary for Norm Epigraphs

children.title: Epigraph Representation Interface
children.top_down_role: Epigraph-based connection between piecewise-linear penalties and LP feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Representation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP interface for the gauge of a polytope given by linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Hz\le\mathbf1\}\) be a bounded polytope with \(0\) in its interior, and define its gauge by \(\gamma_P(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tP\}\). Then \(\gamma_P(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}h_i^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(h_i^{\mathsf T}\) is row \(i\) of \(H\), and \(\operatorname{epi}\gamma_P=\{(x,t):Hx\le t\mathbf1\}\). Thus any minimization model containing \(\gamma_P(Fy+g)\) admits the exact LP interface \(H(Fy+g)\le t\mathbf1\) with objective term \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge of an inequality-described polytope is a finite maximum of row functionals; its epigraph is obtained by scaling every right-hand side by one variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_P(x)=\max_i h_i^{\mathsf T}x\), and \(t\ge\gamma_P(x)\iff Hx\le t\mathbf1\).

notation.meaning: Matrix defining the normalized polytope inequalities.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Representation Size
children.top_down_role: Additional variables and rows introduced by these model families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generator-Lift Formulation and Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-value formula and representation count for a gauge given by finitely many generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) with \(0\in C\), and let \(V=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_k]\). With \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), the extended-valued gauge satisfies \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda:V\lambda=x,\ \lambda\ge0\}.\] The lift uses \(k\) nonnegative auxiliary variables and \(n\) displayed equality rows. It is feasible exactly for \(x\in\operatorname{cone}\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\); whenever feasible, the infimum is attained. Its equality block contains \(\operatorname{nnz}(V)\) nonzeros, and its objective has \(k\) nonzero coefficients before presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-generator gauge has a lift with k nonnegative variables and n displayed equalities; outside the generator cone its extended value is positive infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma_C(x)=\inf\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda:V\lambda=x,\lambda\ge0\},\quad\Delta n_{\mathrm{var}}=k,\quad\Delta m_{\mathrm{eq}}=n.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns are the displayed generators.
Number of nonzero entries in V.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator-Lift Formulation and Size

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facet-Epigraph Formulation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row and auxiliary-variable count for an inequality-described gauge epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Hz\le\mathbf1\}\) have \(m\) displayed inequalities and satisfy the assumptions ensuring \(\gamma_P(z)=\max_i h_i^{\mathsf T}z\). Replacing a minimization term \(\gamma_P(Fy+g)\) by an epigraph variable \(t\) adds one scalar variable and \(m\) inequalities, \(H(Fy+g)\le t\mathbf1\). Before removal of redundant rows, the added coefficient block in variables \((y,t)\) is \([HF\; -\mathbf1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge displayed by m facet inequalities has a direct LP epigraph using one added variable and m added inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The gauge satisfies the assumptions of the inequality-side epigraph interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta n_{\mathrm{var}}=1,\qquad\Delta m_{\mathrm{row}}=m.

notation.meaning: Number of displayed inequalities defining the gauge unit set.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Epigraph Formulation Size
Auxiliary-Variable Representation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts an exact lifted LP representation of a finitely generated polyhedral gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) contain \(0\), let \(V=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_k]\), and define the gauge \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tC\}\). Then
\[\gamma_C(x)=\min_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^k}\left\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:V\lambda=x,\ \lambda\geq0\right\}.\]
Thus the lifted representation uses \(k\) auxiliary scalar variables, \(n\) equality rows, and \(k\) nonnegativity restrictions; its coefficient matrix has \(\operatorname{nnz}(V)+k\) nonzeros when the objective row is counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge generated by k vertices has an exact lift using k nonnegative variables, n equalities, and a coefficient count controlled by the generator matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)=\min\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:V\lambda=x,\ \lambda\geq0\}\), with \(k\) auxiliary variables and \(n\) equality rows.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns are the generators of the polytope.
Number of nonzero entries of V.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Piecewise-Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact epigraph LP formulation for a separable convex piecewise-linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(J_i\) be a nonempty finite set and let \(f_i(s)=\max_{j\in J_i}\{a_{ij}s+b_{ij}\}\). For any polyhedron \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\),
\[\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)=\inf_{x,t}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n t_i:x\in X,\ t_i\geq a_{ij}x_i+b_{ij}\ \text{for all }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\ j\in J_i\right\}.\]
For each feasible \(x\), minimizing over \(t\) sets \(t_i=f_i(x_i)\). Consequently, the projection onto the \(x\)-coordinates of the epigraph formulation's minimizers equals the minimizer set of the original problem, including when both sets are empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable convex piecewise-linear objective has an exact LP epigraph formulation with one epigraph variable per coordinate and one inequality per affine piece; the formulation preserves the infimum and the optimal x-solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(J_i\) is nonempty and finite for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) equals the infimum of the displayed epigraph LP, and the projection of its minimizer set is \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\).

notation.meaning: Nonempty finite index set of affine pieces for coordinate i.
Epigraph variable for the value of the ith component function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Component Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the continuous-LP epigraph construction for separable piecewise-linear objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a piecewise-linear component \(f_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is nonconvex, then \(\operatorname{epi}f_i\) is nonconvex and therefore cannot equal a polyhedron or a coordinate projection of a polyhedron. Thus its full epigraph has no exact formulation using finitely many continuous variables and linear constraints; an exact model generally requires additional disjunctive structure, such as integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex piecewise-linear component has a nonconvex epigraph, so its full epigraph cannot be represented by a finite continuous LP.
assumptions_latex: At least one component \(f_i\) is piecewise linear and nonconvex.
The formulation must reproduce the component's full epigraph using finitely many continuous linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_i\text{ nonconvex}\implies\operatorname{epi}f_i\text{ is not the projection of a finite-dimensional polyhedron}.

notation.meaning: Epigraph of the ith component function.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Component Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composition of Bijective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of objective-preserving bijective recovery under chained reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(T_{12}:X_1\to X_2\) and \(T_{23}:X_2\to X_3\) are bijections with inverses \(S_{21}\) and \(S_{32}\), and satisfy \(f_2(T_{12}(x))=f_1(x)\) and \(f_3(T_{23}(y))=f_2(y)\). Then \(T_{13}=T_{23}\circ T_{12}\) is an objective-preserving bijection with inverse \(S_{31}=S_{21}\circ S_{32}\). Hence bijective solution-recoverability, with specified objective-preserving maps, is an equivalence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-preserving bijective reformulations compose, so bijective recoverability is an equivalence relation.
assumptions_latex: \(T_{12}\) and \(T_{23}\) are objective-preserving bijections between the indicated feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{13}=T_{23}\circ T_{12}\text{ is an objective-preserving bijection with inverse }S_{21}\circ S_{32}.

notation.meaning: Forward recovery map from formulation i to formulation j.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Bijective Reformulations
Bijective Solution-Recovery Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reformulations whose feasible points and objective values correspond one-to-one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\inf\{f(x):x\in X\}\) and \(Q=\inf\{g(y):y\in Y\}\). The formulations are bijectively solution-recoverable if there exist maps \(T:X\to Y\) and \(S:Y\to X\) such that \(S\circ T=\operatorname{id}_X\), \(T\circ S=\operatorname{id}_Y\), and \(g(T(x))=f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently, \(T\) bijects the feasible sets, preserves objective values, and restricts to a bijection between the optimal-solution sets; \(S=T^{-1}\) recovers the original solution uniquely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations have bijective recovery when inverse maps pair every feasible point uniquely and preserve its objective value, hence also pair their optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) bijects \(X\) with \(Y\) and bijects \(\operatorname{argmin}_X f\) with \(\operatorname{argmin}_Y g\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary-Dependent Objective Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates feasible-set projection equivalence from optimization equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\operatorname{proj}_xY\), and define the fiber value \(\phi(x)=\inf\{g(x,z):(x,z)\in Y\}\). Feasible-set projection alone does not make optimization over \(Y\) equivalent to minimizing an intended objective \(f\) over \(X\). Pointwise equality \(\phi(x)=f(x)\) gives equality of infima. Equality of recovered optimizer sets additionally requires that the fiber infimum be attained above every \(x\in\operatorname{argmin}_X f\); this attainment is automatic when \(Y\) is a polyhedron, \(g\) is linear, and the fiber optimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection of feasible sets is insufficient for an auxiliary-dependent objective: fiber minima must reproduce the original objective, and optimal fibers must attain those minima for optimizer recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi(x)=\inf\{g(x,z):(x,z)\in Y\}\) is well-defined as an extended-real value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi=f\text{ on }X\implies\inf_Y g=\inf_X f;\quad \operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}_Yg=\operatorname*{argmin}_Xf\text{ if the relevant fiber infima are attained}.

notation.meaning: Infimum of the lifted objective over the auxiliary fiber above x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transitivity of Projection Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of nested polyhedral lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\), and \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p+q}\) satisfy \(X=\operatorname{proj}_xY\) and \(Y=\operatorname{proj}_{x,z}Z\). Then \(X=\operatorname{proj}_xZ\). If every formulation minimizes the same function of \(x\) alone, their optimal values agree and the projection onto \(x\) of the optimal set over \(Z\) equals the optimal set over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested projection-equivalent lifts compose, and an objective depending only on original variables preserves values and original-variable optimizers.
assumptions_latex: The compared objective depends only on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X=\operatorname{proj}_xZ,\qquad\operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}_{Z}c^{\mathsf T}x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{X}c^{\mathsf T}x.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the second auxiliary-variable block.

knowledge_statements.title: Transitivity of Projection Equivalence
Projection-Equivalent Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an extended formulation by exact projection onto the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of an LP and let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be a polyhedron in variables \((x,z)\). The lifted formulation is projection-equivalent to \(X\) when
\[X=\operatorname{proj}_x(Y)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^p,\ (x,z)\in Y\}.\]
If its objective is \(c^\top x\), independent of \(z\), then the original and lifted LPs have equal optimal values, and the projection of the lifted optimal-solution set equals the original optimal-solution set. Multiple lifted points may recover the same \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted formulation is projection-equivalent when eliminating its auxiliary variables gives exactly the original feasible set; auxiliary solutions need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two LPs have equal optimal values and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{argmin}_{(x,z)\in Y}c^\top x)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in X}c^\top x\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate projection onto the original x-space.
